coursework:
All Coursework, Qualifying Exam, and Dissertation Proposal already complete.
Research: I’m testing whether upward mobility depends on relative standing inside nested talent pools—where the payoff to stronger peer pools is largest through the middle of the hierarchy and weakens at the most elite level, where promotion and opportunity are scarce (a nonlinear pattern: low in weak pools, highest in the middle, and slower/lower at the very top). I established this first in a closed military promotion market (senior-rater evaluation pools, leave–self–out peer quality, officer evaluation-based performance). During this review period I also built a public, replicable college-basketball → NBA draft test (~2011–2021 player–seasons; teammate quality = mean teammate performance with self excluded; draft as the outcome) and found a qualitatively similar “helps in the middle, flattens or falls at the very top” pattern. I am now on the academic/tenure third setting (Computer Science Departments at the top R1 Universities.
other: To ground the sports work in how leagues and teams actually work, I reached out to experts in sports analytics—including an interview with Brian MacDonald (Princeton), who previously led sports analytics at ESPN—to pressure-test our outcome, teammate-quality measure, and data limits, and to ask what might mimic the Army’s constrained top ratings in basketball (e.g. playing time and role on loaded teams). I then scraped, assembled, and fully pipelined the basketball data so the sports analysis is methodologically parallel in spirit to the Army promotion/attrition setup (same leave–self–out peer pool idea; binned readouts; careful comparability across settings), and the basketball and military results line up. Along the way I improved reproducible workflow and sample bookkeeping (who enters/exits the analysis at each step).

Write a journal manuscript for a broad, interdisciplinary audience, framing the same nested-pool idea across the military, sports, and academic settings (with clear notes where estimands differ). Integrate and harden checks for congestion, relative rank and scarcity, and context-driven selection—and prepare defense-ready chapters.

comment:
